newsitem.title: GERMANY: German "wise man" - G7 may intervene to help mark.
newsitem.headline: German "wise man" - G7 may intervene to help mark.

text.p: A leading adviser to the German government said on Tuesday the Group of Seven (G7) industrialised nations' central banks might intervene on foreign exchange markets to support the struggling deutschemark.

In an interview with the German daily Berliner Zeitung, Rolf Peffekoven, a member of the Council of Economic Advisers dubbed Germany's "five wise men," said raising interest rates to support the mark would not be appropriate given German economic weakness but intervention would be an option.
"It is conceiveable that the central banks of the leading industrialised nations will come together on intervention," he told the newspaper.
The mark, which sank to seven-and-a-half year lows against the dollar on Monday, recovered slightly on Tuesday to trade at 1.8350 to the dollar at 1103 GMT.

Pfeffekoven also said the strong dollar and strong pound would create substantial problems for the export sectors of their respective countries, adding that U.S. and Bitish central banks would be carefully watching that impact.
"The two countries will not just watch these developments and do nothing," he said.
